reviews.text:
I hadn't intended to buy a dog, but I wandered into the store and saw a very cute Chihuahua. Immediately, a staff member (Ms. Shiraki) approached us and let us hold the puppy.

Afterward, she listened to our concerns and gave us honest advice based on her own knowledge and experience.

As mentioned above, I initially had no intention of adopting a dog, but the puppy's cuteness, along with Ms. Shiraki's kindness and attentive service, made me seriously consider buying it. I asked her to hold it for me and left the store.

After discussing it, we decided to refrain from buying it this time. We could have simply called to cancel, but because Ms. Shiraki had been so kind, we wanted to visit the store in person to properly apologize and express our gratitude.

Ms. Shiraki didn't show any displeasure at our decision; instead, she let us hold the puppy we wanted to buy, and even escorted us to the exit with the puppy.

Through this experience, I realized that while meeting a dog is certainly important, when it comes to dealing with various issues such as illness and training, the encounter with the store staff—where and from whom you buy the dog—is also crucial.
If there were more store staff like Ms. Shiraki, I believe many more people would be able to live with pets with peace of mind.
Once again, Ms. Shiraki, thank you so much for your wonderful service and for the happy time today.

To the puppy you couldn't take home today... I hope it finds a wonderful family and lives a happy life.

A young female employee was trying to force me to buy a dog.

What does she think dogs and cats are? Was she trying to meet a quota?

I had just dropped in on a whim, not intending to get a pet, and only intended to look.

I happened to see a toy poodle puppy and commented on how cute it was, and she asked, "Would you like to hold it?" I agreed.

I mentioned that I already had a dog at home, and that my family's dog was also a toy poodle. She said, "It looks like it wants to be taken home."

I explained that I already had a dog at home and was just stopping by, and tried to return the puppy, but she said, "This puppy has a cute face, so it will be sold quickly."

She used the puppy's paws to urge me to take it home quickly.

I wanted to leave, so I returned the puppy, but she forced me to exchange LINE contact information, and she sent me pictures of the puppy I had held.

I had only dropped in on a whim, but because of that woman, I ended up staying in the store for nearly 30 minutes.

I've blocked them on LINE as well.

When I said I couldn't keep the dog, they made a clearly displeased face, and I was really angry at their pushy sales tactics.

The store smells strongly of poop and pee.

You can even smell it in the food court next door.

What do they think animals are? Do they have some kind of quota to meet? Since then, I've been avoiding going inside because I feel like I'll be subjected to pushy sales tactics, so I just look at the dogs from outside.

I recommend not just casually walking in.

A male staff member was teaching a female staff member how to feed the dogs and cats, and he was saying things like, "Dogs are stupid, so they'll eat it all if you give them to them, but cats..." which I found really off-putting. Aren't they supposed to be working there because they love dogs and cats? It makes me question their character. There wasn't even a "welcome" when I entered the store, and they were completely unfriendly.

I visited again, but was disappointed.
---
The prices are high, but there are many cute pets and they're in good health, so it's easy to find one you like. Due to its location, it feels like a flagship store. Also, compared to other pet shops, there's less of a pushy sales tactic. I actually found one I liked here and bought it. It's healthy and growing up to be a good pet.

The dogs always seem to be having fun. lol
The staff are always friendly and helpful, so I feel at ease.

I often come here to relieve stress.
Today's cats were just as cute as ever.
I'll come again.

A female employee with light brown hair tied back with a hair clip suddenly told my daughter, "You can't wear shoes inside, so please stop," even though my daughter was just sitting still on the sofa with her feet down.

I don't understand why she said that to me, as my daughter wasn't making any noise and wasn't even standing on the chair with her shoes on.

Unfortunately dogs at stores come from puppy mills (look it up). Dog Moms are birthing multiple litters in poor environments and then their babies are being separated young. The only way around this is to visit the house of a breeder or to adopt a dog from a shelter.
The staff were nice. However, the smell inside the store bothered me.
Rude staff.

A clean and spacious store.

The staff are enthusiastic, but quite pushy with their sales pitches.

It stinks. The smell of excrement, cheap dog food, and perfume is leaking into the food court.

All the other pet shops use deodorizing air purifiers, so why is this store the only one that hasn't had one since opening?

It's a nuisance, so I hope they do something about it.

I often come here to relieve stress.
Today's cats were just as cute as ever.
I'll come again.
There are so many adorable puppies here, each one irresistibly cute—I almost wish I could take them home!

All the puppies here are cute and above a certain standard. I got the impression that there were a lot of mixed breed puppies.
It's true that over 500,000 yen is the norm, but there are also cute puppies over 3 months old that cost around 200,000 yen, so depending on the person, this might be a good option. If there are no problems, you can apparently adopt one on the same day, so it's great to have that fateful encounter.
If I'm going to pay around 2,000 to 3,000 dollars, I expect attention and care from the store staff. I wouldn't pay 3,000 dollars for this kind of service.”
Perhaps because they were selling rescue dogs on the floor above, this store was selling sick cats.

The dogs and cats are kept in transparent cases, allowing you to view them from various angles.

When a dog pooped, the staff quickly took care of it, showing that they are being treated with care.

This chain is far too expensive.

I don't think the price is worth it at all.
Also, and this isn't limited to this pet shop, but the puppies and kittens are far too young.
There are many other breeders who will sell you puppies and kittens at a more reasonable price, allowing them to spend time with their parents and siblings until the appropriate age, develop proper socialization, and undergo thorough health checks and genetic disease testing.
Which is better: buying a puppy here for 500,000 to 1,000,000 yen that has been separated from its parents and siblings too early for the sake of temporary cuteness, crammed with unfamiliar dogs, and subjected to the stress of being stared at by strangers every day, or a puppy that has been separated from its parents and siblings too early for the sake of temporary cuteness?
I want you to think about this again.

I visited the store with a friend.

So many selections

All the animals looked healthy.
However, some were priced at over 1 million yen. I was shocked! I couldn't afford them, though...
The cutest things I've ever seen. Amazing and beautiful dogs and cats. The price is quite high, but you get the most beautiful animals.
